why: I checked both verifier checks against their expect lines. Check 1 passes when "the --tsv command prints a JSON array equal to the array the plain command prints for the CSV form of the same table." It fails on an error, on output that is not an array, or on a mismatch. That is what "the same JSON array" requires. Comparing the outputs as parsed JSON keeps it lenient. The phrase "rows keyed by the header row" adds nothing in practice: the plain command already keys rows by the header ('[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]'), so equal arrays are keyed too. Check 2 passes when README mentions `--tsv` and either says it is for tab-separated input or shows it in a usage example. That is a fair reading of "documents." The stricter tests are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail)": `npm test` passing, a new test being added, and byte-for-byte output with the trailing newline. No PASS or FAIL condition demands a mutation test, a branch rule or exact wording.
